answer: Slashable sponsorship resists cheap-wallet floods. A newcomer joins only after a trusted peer locks a bond and co-signs enrollment. If later clustering proves the account is fake, that bond is burned and the sponsor loses invite rights. An attacker who wants a thousand identities must bribe a thousand sponsors or grow a self-funded tree over many epochs, paying capital and reputation at every layer. Growth is no faster than a living reef adding calcium. The bond sits in public view like a relic on a busy wharf, so anyone can see who signed and whether it was slashed.
